Lab Objectives
1. Identify the right coronary artery and its branches (e.g., right marginal, posterior
interventricular/PDA).
2. Identify the left coronary artery and its branches (e.g., anterior interventricular/LAD, circumflex).
3. Differentiate between right and left dominant coronary circulation.
4. Identify the coronary sinus and its tributaries (great, middle, and small cardiac veins).
5. Locate the anatomical position of the sinoatrial (SA) node in relation to the sulcus terminalis and
the junction of the superior vena cava with the right atrium.
6. Locate the anatomical position of the atrioventricular (AV) node and identify its arterial supply.
7. Identify the atrioventricular bundle (of His) and its right and left bundle branches.
8. Relate the territory supplied by each coronary artery to the common sites of myocardial infarction
and to the blood supply of the conducting system.

Right Coronary Artery
Right aortic sinus
Arises from the right (coronary) aortic sinus. Smaller than the left. Courses anteriorly and toward the
right between the right atrial appendage and pulmonary trunk, then runs almost vertically downward
between the right atrium and right ventricle in the coronary sulcus. Turns posteriorly to continue on the
diaphragmatic surface of the heart on the right. Gives off several branches:
Arch of aorta
Ascending aorta

Anterior cardiac
veins
1) Atrial branch, which gives off sinuatrial (SA) nodal branch that supplies the sinuatrial node.
2) Anterior atrial and ventricular branches supplying the right atrium and right ventricle.
3) Right (acute) marginal branch, which courses along the right (acute) margin of the heart and
supplies the right ventricle.
4) Branch to the atrioventricular (AV) node as it courses along the diaphragmatic surface of
the heart.
5) Posterior interventricular (posterior descending): final major branch that lies in the
posterior interventricular sulcus and supplies the right and left ventricles on their diaphragmatic
surface and the posterior one-third of the interventricular septum.

Coronary artery bypass grafting CABG
Patients with obstruction of their coronary circulation and severe angina may undergo a coronary bypass graft operation. A segment of an artery or vein is connected to
the ascending aorta or to the proximal part of a coronary artery and then to the coronary artery distal to the stenosis. The great saphenous vein and internal thoracic
artery are commonly harvested vessels for coronary bypass surgery.
CVP-Lab-2

The Cardiac Veins
The veins draining the heart essentially follow the coronary arteries but are named differently. Almost all the veins drain into the
coronary sinus, a large venous channel located in the coronary sulcus on the posterior aspect of the heart that empties into the
right atrium. The coronary sinus receives four major tributaries:
1. Great cardiac vein
Begins near the apex of the heart and ascends with the LAD in the anterior interventricular sulcus.
Turns left at the coronary sulcus and accompanies the circumflex artery to the back of the heart
and enlarges in the posterior aspect of the coronary sulcus into the coronary sinus, which opens
into the right atrium. Drains the anterior aspects of the right and left ventricles and
interventricular septum.
• Anterior interventricular artery (LAD)
3. Small cardiac vein
Begins as the right marginal vein. Drains right portion of
right ventricle and opens into the coronary sinus
Coronary sinus
4. Posterior cardiac vein (posterior vein of the left ventricle): on posterior aspect of
left ventricle to the left of the middle cardiac vein. Drains posterior aspect of left
ventricle and opens into the coronary sinus.
5. Anterior cardiac veins: small veins arising on the anterior aspect of the right
ventricle, crossing the coronary sulcus and opening directly into the right atrium.
6. Thebesian veins: the smallest of the cardiac veins draining directly into the heart
chambers.

2. Middle cardiac vein
Begins near the apex and ascends in the posterior interventricular sulcus with the posterior interventricular
artery and opens into the coronary sinus. Drains the posterior aspects of the right and left ventricles and
interventricular septum.
